short: first word of a passage after a lead-in line
notes:
Card: max 15.4, density 0.30%, peaks 'The' x5, ' It', 'For', 'To', '2' (Retrieved ... 2012) at the first token after a newline that follows a speaker label ('BRANDON RITTIMAN: It'), a title line ('The Epistle Dedicatory'), or 'Krugman wrote:'. Probe: 'Paul Krugman wrote:
For all the talk' 0.266 (peak 'For'), 'From the preface to the 1674 edition.
The reader' 0.117, 'civil society:
To civil society' 0.070, 'REPORTER: It was' 0.047; inline 'wrote that for all' 0.038, bare sentences 0.032-0.040, 'Retrieved 12 March 2015' 0.047. The direction is right but the values are small, so the test uses longer lead-ins (column attribution, dedication, transcript label, chapter heading, reader's question) with the body on the next line; near misses run the same words inline in one sentence.
